sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆，这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: One of the great things about science is that it can change the way we see the world.
sentences.zh: 科学最伟大的地方之一，在于它能改变我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: Today, we have an episode from March 2017 that I still think about all the time.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们带来一期2017年3月的节目，我至今仍常常想起它。

sentences.en: It's a story that will change the way you think about many things.
sentences.zh: 这是一个将改变你对许多事物看法的真实故事。
贫困、孤独、时间，甚至饥饿。

sentences.en: It's a tale about the psychological phenomenon of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于稀缺的心理学现象的故事。

sentences.en: It affects nearly everything in our lives
sentences.zh: 它几乎影响着我们生活中的方方面面，

sentences.en: and connects people who appear to have nothing in common.
sentences.zh: 并将那些看似毫无共同点的人们联系在一起。

sentences.en: The story of scarcity is a story of how not having enough of what you need
sentences.zh: 关于稀缺的故事，讲述的是当你缺乏所需之物时，

sentences.en: can become the only thing that matters to you.
sentences.zh: 这种缺乏如何变成对你而言唯一重要的事情。

sentences.en: That, I think, is the basic scarcity instinct.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是最基本的稀缺本能。

sentences.en: And then this thing starts going off in the head saying,
sentences.zh: 然后大脑里就会开始有声音说：

sentences.en: The Scarcity Trap, this week on Hidden Brain.

sentences.zh: 我来自密歇根州底特律。

sentences.en: Brandy Drew has a story that may sound familiar to you.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪·德鲁有一个你听起来可能会觉得熟悉的故事。

sentences.en: A story of poverty and debt.
sentences.zh: 一个关于贫穷与债务的故事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of story that may lead people to quick conclusions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很容易让人下意识得出结论的故事。

sentences.en: So pay attention to your own.
sentences.zh: 所以请留意你自己的想法。

sentences.en: Six years ago, her life unraveled.
sentences.zh: 六年前，她的生活分崩离析。

sentences.en: At the time, she ran the dining services department at a senior living facility.
sentences.zh: 当时，她在一家高级生活服务设施管理餐饮服务部门。

sentences.en: She'd been with a company that ran it for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 她在这家运营该设施的公司工作了十多年。

sentences.en: One day, she made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她犯了一个错误。

sentences.en: I was just in a rush to get home.
It was like maybe a 10-mile drive, busy traffic area.
sentences.zh: 开车大概有10英里路，而且交通非常拥堵。

sentences.en: And I knew I had to pick up diapers.
sentences.zh: 我知道我必须去买尿布。

sentences.en: And the easiest thing for me, I thought, would be to pick them up before I picked the baby up.
sentences.zh: 我想最省事的方法，就是在接孩子之前先把尿布买好。

sentences.en: So Brandy stopped at a store, ran in, and grabbed the diapers.
sentences.zh: 于是布兰迪在一家商店停下，跑进去拿了尿布。

sentences.en: She swiped her credit card at the self-checkout station and raced out.
sentences.zh: 她在自助结账台刷了信用卡，然后匆忙离开。

sentences.en: It turns out she used the wrong card.
Not her own, but the company credit card.
sentences.zh: 用的不是她自己的卡，而是公司信用卡。

sentences.en: But what's crazy is I didn't realize at that moment, I didn't realize until my supervisor called me in and said,
sentences.zh: 但疯狂的是，我当时根本没意识到，直到我的主管把我叫去说：

sentences.en: So had she not said anything, I don't think I would have realized that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果她没说起，我想我根本不会意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Brandy carried the card in case she needed to buy dining supplies for work.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪随身带着这张卡，以防工作时需要购买餐饮用品。

sentences.en: She'd never had a problem before, never been reprimanded.
sentences.zh: 她以前从未出过问题，也从未受过训诫。

sentences.en: She thought an apology and an explanation would do.
sentences.zh: 她以为道个歉、解释一下就行了。

sentences.en: And her response was, well, you know, we have to terminate you.
sentences.zh: 而对方的反应是，嗯，你知道的，我们不得不解雇你。

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, I didn't know that.
Like, can I just pay you back?
sentences.zh: 我说，我能把钱还给你们吗？

sentences.en: And she said, no, in cases like that, you automatically have to terminate the employee.
sentences.zh: 她说，不行，遇到这种情况下，你必须自动被解雇。

sentences.en: I cried for like a whole day because I couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我哭了整整一天，因为我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I didn't want to go home and tell my kids what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想回家告诉孩子们发生了什么。

sentences.en: I didn't want to tell my husband what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想告诉丈夫发生了什么。

sentences.en: I just didn't know what to do at that point.
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道当时该怎么办。

sentences.en: I felt like a failure as a parent because I didn't provide a good example, even though
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己作为一个父母很失败，因为我没有树立好榜样，尽管

sentences.en: Brandy earned more than her husband, so the loss of the job hit hard.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪的收入比丈夫高，因此失去工作对她的打击沉重。
她觉得自己是个失败者。

sentences.en: She tried to bring in money doing odd jobs like cooking takeaway meals, but the stress
sentences.zh: 她尝试做一些零工来赚钱，比如烹制外卖餐食，但压力

sentences.en: Brandy and her husband began fighting.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪和丈夫开始争吵。

sentences.en: She had supported him when he'd been laid off a few years earlier, and she'd expected
sentences.zh: 几年前他失业时，她曾支持过他，她本期望

sentences.en: he'd do the same for her.
But he felt a layoff was different.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得失业是不一样的。

sentences.en: He was mad that she'd made a stupid mistake.
sentences.zh: 他很生气她犯了这么蠢的错误。

sentences.en: The final argument was that I left out the house that morning.
sentences.zh: 最后一次争吵的起因是我那天早上出门。

sentences.en: I was going to job interviews.
I had two interviews that day, and I didn't purchase toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 我那天有两场面试，而我没有买卫生纸。

sentences.en: So when he got home from work that day, there was no toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 所以他那天工下班回家时，家里没有卫生纸。

sentences.en: When I came in with the kids, he just immediately started yelling, you can't keep yourself together.
sentences.zh: 我和孩子一进门，他就立刻大吼大叫，说你连自己都管不好。

sentences.en: So I walked right back out the door, and I never looked back.
sentences.zh: 于是我转身又走出了大门，再也没有回头。

sentences.en: Without steady employment and a husband to help with bills, Brandy watched anxiously
sentences.zh: 没有了稳定的工作和帮忙分担账单的丈夫，布兰迪焦虑地看着
家里的日用品一天天减少。

sentences.en: To make ends meet, she ordered a new credit card.
sentences.zh: 为了勉强维持生计，她申请了一张新信用卡。

sentences.en: The day it arrived, Brandy tore open the envelope.
sentences.zh: 卡一到手，布兰迪就撕开信封。

sentences.en: She grabbed the card and ran out the door.
I went straight to Walmart, and I bought, like, a family size of toilet paper, family size of laundry detergent.
sentences.zh: 我直接去了沃尔玛，买了一大箱家庭装的卫生纸、家庭装的洗衣液。

sentences.en: Like, I stocked up on things all at once, rather than keeping it handy just in case.
sentences.zh: 就像是一次性把东西囤够，而不是只留备用。

sentences.en: So I, like, maxed it out within the first couple of days that I had it, rather than holding on to it for emergency purposes.
sentences.zh: 所以拿到卡的前几天，我就直接把它刷爆了，而不是把它留作紧急备用。

sentences.en: And in that moment, as she was maxing out the credit card on the household supplies she needed,
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，当她把信用卡刷爆来购买生活必需品时，

sentences.en: Brandy forgot about things that were slightly less pressing.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪把那些稍微不那么紧迫的事情抛到了脑后。

sentences.en: What I didn't think about is, what about gas money?
sentences.zh: 我没有考虑的是，油钱怎么办？

sentences.en: I didn't consider what gas would coSt.
sentences.zh: 我没有考虑汽油要花多少钱。

sentences.en: That was, like, the biggest thing.
It was always hard to have gas.
And, of course, there was the credit card bill itself.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有信用卡本身的账单。

sentences.en: The first two months, I paid the minimum payment, and then I just stopped paying, because I couldn't afford to pay.
sentences.zh: 前两个月，我只还了最低还款额，然后就索性不还了，因为我根本付不起。

sentences.en: I didn't pay that card off until I got my tax refund the following year.
sentences.zh: 直到第二年拿到退税，我才把那张卡的欠款还清。

sentences.en: By the time I paid it off, it was over $800 for a $500 card.
sentences.zh: 等我还清时，一张500美元额度的卡已经欠了800多美元。

sentences.en: More and more, Brandy felt trapped by debt.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪越来越深地感到自己被债务困住。

sentences.en: It came down to pay the bills or feed the kids.
sentences.zh: 归根结底就是交账单还是喂饱孩子。

sentences.en: It's just overwhelming trying to juggle all of those things and still maintain a certain state of mind so that my children wouldn't see me struggle.
sentences.zh: 要兼顾所有这些事情，还要保持某种心态不让孩子们看到我的挣扎，这实在太让人崩溃了。

sentences.en: In retrospect, Brandy can see the mistakes she made.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，布兰迪能看到自己犯下的错误。

sentences.en: If she had made a budget for the whole month, she might have remembered she needed to account for gas.
sentences.zh: 如果她做了一个全月的预算，她或许就会记得把油钱算进去。

sentences.en: If she had focused on the big picture, she might not have maxed out a credit card she couldn't afford to pay back.
sentences.zh: 如果她把眼光放长远，她可能就不会刷爆一张自己根本无力偿还的信用卡了。

sentences.en: Why did Brandy make these mistakes?
sentences.zh: 为什么布兰迪会犯这些错误？

sentences.en: It's easy to say she was being irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易说她不负责任。

sentences.en: She had always been careful and conscientious.
sentences.zh: 她一直以来都是一个小心谨慎、认真负责的人。

sentences.en: Did something cause her to behave differently?
sentences.zh: 是有什么原因导致她的行为发生了变化吗？

sentences.en: When you have scarcity and it creates a scarcity mindset, it leads you to take certain behaviors which, in the short term, help you manage scarcity, but in the long term,
sentences.zh: 当你遭遇稀缺并因此产生稀缺心态时，它会促使你采取某些行为，这些行为在短期内有助于应对稀缺，但在长期来看，

sentences.en: When we come back, how the scarcity trap changes the way we think.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨稀缺陷阱如何改变我们的思维方式。

sentences.en: After she lost her job, Brandy fell deeper and deeper into debt.
sentences.zh: 失去工作后，布兰迪陷入了越来越深的债务泥潭。

sentences.en: One big reason is that she made a series of decisions that improved her life in the moment, but made it worse in the long run.
sentences.zh: 一个主要原因在于，她做出了一系列决定：这些决定在当下改善了她的生活，但从长远来看却让生活雪上加霜。

sentences.en: She could have used the new credit card only for emergencies, but instead, she maxed it out in a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 她本可以只在紧急情况下使用新信用卡，但她却在几天内将其刷爆。

sentences.en: To understand why she did this, I want to take you to a completely different time and place,
sentences.zh: 为了理解她为什么这样做，我想带你回到一个完全不同的时代和地点，

sentences.en: because it reveals something important about Brandy's story.
sentences.zh: 因为这揭示了布兰迪的故事中一些重要的东西。

sentences.en: World War II is nearing its end.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战接近尾声。

sentences.en: Europe is on the verge of mass famine.
sentences.zh: 欧洲正处于大规模饥荒的边缘。

sentences.en: Aid workers desperately need guidance on how to bring people back from the brink of starvation.
sentences.zh: 救援人员迫切需要指导，以了解如何将人们从饥饿的边缘拯救回来。

sentences.en: Researchers at the University of Minnesota thought they could help.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达大学的研究人员认为他们可以帮上忙。
他们发起了一项为期一年的实验。

sentences.en: As a 2002 documentary made by the university explains,
sentences.zh: 正如该大学2002年制作的一部纪录片所解释的，

sentences.en: the volunteers were conscientious objectors who still wanted to serve their country.
sentences.zh: 这些志愿者是拒绝服兵役者，但他们仍然希望为国家服务。

sentences.en: The volunteers had to go on a starvation diet.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们必须进行饥饿饮食。

sentences.en: Thirty-six young men, most of them Quakers, Mennonites, or Church of Brethren members,
sentences.zh: 三十六名年轻男子，大多是贵格会教徒、门诺会教徒或弟兄会成员，

sentences.en: moved into the South Tower of the Memorial Stadium, which would be their home for a year.
sentences.zh: 搬进了纪念体育场的南塔，这里将是他们一年的家。

sentences.en: Many took courses at the university, even as they grew thinner and thinner.
sentences.zh: 许多人在大学里上课，尽管他们日渐消瘦。

sentences.en: The young men became walking scarecrows.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻人成了行走的稻草人。

sentences.en: Some grew so weak and bony, they couldn't sit without cushions or raise their arms to wash their hair.
sentences.zh: 有些人变得虚弱骨感，甚至不坐垫子就无法坐下，或者连抬起胳膊洗头都做不到。

sentences.en: I remember being a little bit critical of guys in the early part who had licked their plates.
sentences.zh: 我记得在早期时，我对那些舔盘子的家伙有点苛刻。

sentences.en: I thought that was really pretty crude.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那真的挺粗俗的。

sentences.en: Henry Schoelberg was one of the volunteers.
sentences.zh: 亨利·舍尔伯格是志愿者之一。

sentences.en: He recalled the experience in the documentary.
sentences.zh: 他在纪录片中回忆了这段经历。

sentences.en: By the time we were into about the second month of it, I was doing it myself.
sentences.zh: 大概到了第二个月的时候，我自己也这么做了。

sentences.en: You just needed every single calorie you could get your hand on.
sentences.zh: 你只需要你所能弄到的每一卡路里热量。

sentences.en: The results of the starvation experiment were eventually published and remain an important academic reference on nutrition, famine, and eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 这项饥饿实验的结果最终得以发表，并成为营养学、饥荒和进食障碍方面重要的学术参考。

sentences.en: But recently, two researchers became intrigued with the 70-year-old study for a completely different reason.
sentences.zh: 但最近，两位研究人员出于完全不同的原因对这项已有70年历史的研究产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: They were interested in what the lack of food did, not to the body, but to the mind.
sentences.zh: 他们感兴趣的不是食物短缺对身体造成的影响，而是对心理的影响。

sentences.en: I think this type of scarcity is almost like an alarm that goes off in the head that's saying,
sentences.zh: 我认为这种稀缺几乎就像是在大脑中响起的一个警报，在说：

sentences.en: hey, we really need this thing addressed.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们真的需要解决这个问题。

sentences.en: We really need this thing addressed.
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要解决这个问题。

sentences.en: This is Sendhil Mulayanathan, a professor of computation and behavioral science at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这是森迪尔·穆拉纳坦，芝加哥大学计算与行为科学教授。

sentences.en: He and a colleague, Eldar Shafir, a psychology professor at Princeton, had a theory brewing.
sentences.zh: 他和普林斯顿大学心理学教授埃尔达·沙菲尔当时正在酝酿一个理论。

sentences.en: When you feel that something important is missing in your life, your brain starts to focus on that missing thing.
sentences.zh: 当你觉得生活中缺少了某个重要的东西时，你的大脑就会开始专注于那个缺失的东西。

sentences.en: When you're really desperate for something, you can focus on it so obsessively, there's no room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 当你极度渴望某样东西时，你会全神贯注到痴迷的地步，以至于容不下其他任何东西。

sentences.en: The researchers were just beginning to explore their hypothesis when a colleague mentioned the long-ago Minnesota starvation experiment.
sentences.zh: 研究人员正准备探讨他们的假设时，一位同事提到了很久以前的明尼苏达饥饿实验。

sentences.en: Eldar remembers being immediately fascinated by the study and how the lack of food affected the minds of the men.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达回忆说，自己立刻就被这项研究以及食物短缺如何影响这群男人的心理所吸引。

sentences.en: They basically were very hungry and couldn't stop thinking about eating.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上非常饥饿，满脑子想的都是吃。

sentences.en: In some sense, you'd think, given that they cannot eat, they'd rather be distracted with other things.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你会觉得，既然他们吃不到东西，他们宁愿被别的事情转移注意力。

sentences.en: But in fact, both subconsciously, the level of immediate reaction and their choice of conversation largely was around food.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，无论是下意识的即时反应水平，还是他们的对话选择，很大程度上都围绕着食物。

sentences.en: But actually, it was sort of tragicomic.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这有点像悲喜剧。

sentences.en: I mean, they planned to open restaurants, to become restaurateurs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们计划开餐馆，成为餐馆老板。

sentences.en: They compared food prices at different newspapers.
sentences.zh: 他们在不同的报纸上比较食物价格。
他们当时就在做这些事。

sentences.en: The whole time, they sat around looking at food-related issues.
sentences.zh: 他们整天坐在一起，关注与食物相关的问题。
就连刻意的转移注意力也无济于事。

sentences.en: Hunger and food had captured their minds.
sentences.zh: 饥饿和食物占据了他们的头脑。

sentences.en: At some point, the experimenters just felt sore for them and decided to distract them with a movie.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，实验人员只是替他们感到难过，决定用一部电影来分散他们的注意力。

sentences.en: And some of the testimonials were, they showed me this movie.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人的反馈是，他们给我看了这部电影。

sentences.en: I couldn't care less about the love scenes.
sentences.zh: 我对爱情戏一点兴趣都没有。

sentences.en: I wanted to see the meals.
Eldar suddenly realized he had seen the same kind of behavior in a completely different setting.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达突然意识到，他在一个完全不同的环境中见过这种行为。

sentences.en: He'd done a lot of research on the effects of poverty,
sentences.zh: 他做过大量关于贫困影响的研究，

sentences.en: and he knew poor people who sometimes behaved like the starving men in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 他认识的一些穷人，有时表现得就像明尼苏达州的饥饿男青年一样。

sentences.en: The poor, people who were lacking financial resources,
sentences.zh: 穷人，即缺乏财务资源的人，

sentences.en: found it very hard to think about anything but money,
sentences.zh: 发现自己很难去想别的事情，满脑子都是钱，

sentences.en: or at least spend a lot of their cognitive resources, a lot of their attention, on financial juggling.
sentences.zh: 或者至少把大量的认知资源、大量的注意力都花在了应付财务上。

sentences.en: If starvation made people obsess over food,
sentences.zh: 如果饥饿让人对食物念念不忘，

sentences.en: poverty made people obsess over how they were going to make ends meet,
sentences.zh: 那么贫困就会让人纠结于如何维持生计，

sentences.en: how to make it to next week.
What's in common in both cases is your head is busy with a thing you don't have enough of.
sentences.zh: 这两种情况的共同点是，你的脑子里一直想着你所缺乏的东西。

sentences.en: The two researchers felt they were on to something.
sentences.zh: 两位研究人员觉得他们有了重大发现。

sentences.en: Maybe, they thought, the human brain is wired to respond to scarcity
